questions.question: How many lighthouses in the table have no event at all in the events file, counting an undated event as an event?
questions.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM lighthouses l WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM events e WHERE e.lighthouse.qid = l.qid)
questions.note: The table has 80 lighthouses; the events file has 62 events, but they belong to only 46 distinct lighthouses (many have two or three events, e.g. Bishop Rock three, Lundy North three), so 80 - 46 = 34 lighthouses have no event. The tempting wrong answer is 80 - 62 = 18, which subtracts event rows instead of distinct lighthouses. Every event's lighthouse is a row of the table, so no event is lost on the join; undated events (Lizard, Start Point, Peninnis, ...) still count as events, so their lighthouses are not among the 34. Re-derived by (SELECT count(*) FROM lighthouses) - (SELECT count(DISTINCT lighthouse.qid) FROM events) and by a NOT IN on the name column: 34 each time.

questions.question: Which lighthouses does the table record as entering service in a later year than their inception year, comparing only the year even where a cell gives a month or a full date?
questions.sql: SELECT name FROM lighthouses WHERE CAST(substr(service_entry, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) > CAST(substr(inception, 1, 4) AS INTEGER)
questions.note: Eight rows, found by comparing the first four characters of two mixed-precision columns: Hartland Point (1874 to 2012), Bull Point (1879 to 1974), Portland Bill (1903 to 1906), St Bees (1822 to 1867), Belle Tout (1832 to 1834), Europa Point (1838 to 1841-08-01), Helgoland (1810 to 1811-02) and Bishop Rock (1858 to 1887). Two traps. First, a plain string comparison of the cells gives 12: it adds Pendeen (1900 vs 1900-10-03), Trevose Head (1847 vs 1847-12-01), Flamborough Head (1806 vs 1806-12-01) and Souter (1871 vs 1871-01-11), where a full date sorts after the same bare year although the year is equal; Godrevy (inception 1859-03-01, service entry 1859) and Royal Sovereign (both 1971-09-06) are equal years too. Second, counting every row whose two cells differ gives 10: Winterton (1867 to 1840) and Orfordness (1793 to 1792) entered service in an earlier year, not a later one. Rows with an empty inception or service entry cell (48 of the 80) cannot be compared and are out. Re-derived by padding each cell to a full date, casting it to DATE and comparing year(): the same eight names.
